column8: Storage metric sample is an int64 gauge callback: EdgeCount errors produce its defined unavailable sample value, not a query collection or command acknowledgement. The request handlers that publish authoritative counts are separate members.

Storage metric node-count probe implements the telemetry sampler’s scalar-only interface; its zero fallback does not authorize a data-read consumer to discard errors. This member has no query or mutation result terminal.
Independent batch/point oracle deliberately has no Go error return: it asserts both returned errors and values with testing.Require. No failed read is treated as a successful product result.

Stored mode test adapter asserts successful modes or explicit ErrNotImplemented refusal before accessing facts; this is an executable test oracle, not an errorless product API.

The remote peer test helper has a testing.T contract and immediately asserts the point error before updating the marker. Its void signature delegates failure to the test oracle; no production caller accepts a failed storage read as success.

The CREATE/MATCH ID seek is optional: a failed bound getQueryNode yields an unresolved variable, so tryResolveMatchBindingsFromIDPredicates returns handled=false unless all variables were independently resolved. The general MATCH path remains authoritative; this helper cannot acknowledge a failed seek as handled empty data.
Simple MATCH/LIMIT optimization declines on collection failure (nil,false); it does not return handled empty success. The ordinary statement path remains responsible for the read/error terminal.

An indexed hit whose required hydration fails now declines the entire optimization, preserving genuine not-found filtering. The query router retries its ordinary MATCH owner; partial scores are never delivered as handled.

Exact cosine scoring without a label treats AllNodes failure as handled=false. Optimizer callers fall back to the ordinary query; the standalone vector procedure turns false into a query error. Neither accepts a handled empty score set after this failure.

The label-restricted exact cosine branch returns handled=false on GetNodesByLabel error before scoring. Its caller either performs the ordinary read or emits the procedure query error; a failed label read is never a successful zero-hit exact result.

Filtered exact cosine scoring admits the optional full-node scan only when AllNodes succeeds. Failure refuses the optimization with false, preserving the general query's read/error terminal rather than treating missing scan data as a completed result.

The filtered label-specific cosine branch rejects the optimization on GetNodesByLabel error. The bool carries optimizer admission, not storage success; only a successful scan reaches its filtering and score output.
Relationship score fast path can recover an index-query failure with the exact edge scan. If that scan fails it declines the optimization, leaving the ordinary execution path to report failure.

Required relationship or endpoint read failure now declines this direct-return optimization; only genuine absence filters a hit. Its router then uses ordinary MATCH, retaining the issued view and statement terminal.

The WITH/projection variant now rejects its whole tentative result on a hard edge/context read failure; no accumulated prefix of rows is marked handled. Ordinary query execution owns recovery and terminal errors.
DELETE return projection records a required point-read error in the existing expression-failure context, which the statement terminal checks; an invalid identity is rejected before the read.

Graph identity in-degree is a legacy public Engine method with no error channel. Its degree body is preserved and Deprecated; internal data consumers must use the error-returning adjacency owner.
Graph identity out-degree keeps its public int signature and zero-on-failure behavior. Its doc names GetOutgoingEdges; it is not permitted as an internal query consumer.
Link-prediction semantic callback records a hard point failure in the active statement expression-failure owner, and later callbacks stop reading after that terminal is set.

The native graph degree callback invokes getNodeEdges on the identity-view executor and records a read failure in the existing expression terminal before returning its numeric placeholder. Catalog projections instead use their already captured relationship set.

Ordered-group hydration writes hard point failures to visitErr and stops the callback. The outer operation returns that error before any candidate window can be accepted; actual not-found continues to filter stale index IDs.

Chained MATCH records a loadPatternNodes error in the execution context before returning its legacy slice pair. The pipeline shares that context and the outer expression/public terminal reads the recorded failure, so the nil bindings cannot become a successful empty MATCH.

A failed cache validation evicts the cached candidate and returns no match; findExistingMergeNode continues to the schema/label source query. The failed validation neither binds the stale holder nor authorizes a create before the ordinary lookup.

StorageExecutor.BatchGetNodes is the documented map-only compatibility wrapper over BatchGetNodesContext; successful IDs remain while failed IDs are omitted. Its production internal-consumer compiler proof passed 3d5d onba91.

Public optimizer preserves its handled bool protocol: the corrected point cache error produces nil,false, so no unrecovered failure is accepted as a handled empty result. Both-parser public green is on285642447.

Edge-property aggregation now binds the issued point adapter once, propagates cache failures and reads issued edges; BEGIN/failure/healthy/missing schedules passed both parsers on285642447.
Directed count aggregation uses the same issued edge and point owners and carries point failures; both incoming and outgoing public schedules passed both parsers on285642447.

Path-search relationship callback explicitly records walk/combine failure in the existing statement expression terminal before returning no edges; a void callback does not become successful query data.

Uniform path hydration uses the issued-view error-returning batch owner. On failure it refuses the uniform optimization; pair then performs the general path search, whose point reads preserve hard errors through the expression terminal. A recovered ordinary read may answer, but the failed batch cannot be accepted as a completed empty uniform result.
Row refresh uses the statement’s existing expression-failure owner when a hard fresh read fails; returning the old row cannot erase that terminal error.

Bound degree expression already records adjacency read failure in the statement error terminal; the numeric placeholder is not a public successful result. Corrected public control is pending collection.

Labelless property-index count is optional planning admission: failure returns false and declines the index shortcut. The ordinary label/node reader then computes the result through an error-bearing owner.

The legacy int-only API counts w.GetIncomingEdges on its issued transaction, preserving pending data. Zero on a failed read is the documented compatibility exception; compiled unavailability proves no product consumer calls the legacy API.

The legacy int-only API counts w.GetOutgoingEdges on its issued transaction instead of the committed base. Its documented zero-on-failure compatibility remains restricted to external callers by the compiler population gate.

Traversal incident-edge failure is recorded in cancelCtx, the existing statement failure carrier; production traversal construction supplies that context. No new traversal capture or reader owner is added.

Traversal endpoint hydration uses the bound relationship endpoint reader. A hard error is recorded in cancelCtx before returning false; not-found remains a visibility outcome. Public path evaluation checks that same expression failure and cannot publish a valid-looking empty traversal.
Traversal header and adjacency reads already record the selected read error into cancelCtx. The returned list is internal work only; statement completion checks that same terminal.

Relationship-ID seed materialization records hard read failures in the existing statement expression-failure owner; absent relationships remain legitimate omitted seeds.

GraphBuilder worker reports the first adjacency failure via sync.Once, waits for every worker, then returns the error; no worker-local void signature loses the public Build error.

Embedding claim preserves an unreadable candidate in pending/retry state and returns no claimed work; only confirmed nodeGone removes it. It does not publish a successful read result or acknowledge an embedding.

Embedding claim preserves an unreadable candidate in pending/retry state and returns no claimed work; only confirmed nodeGone removes it. It does not publish a successful read result or acknowledge an embedding.

Permanent embedding-failure administration first obtains the current node. A hard read failure returns without marking the queue entry completed; only nodeGone removes an already absent node. The background attempt owner retains retry responsibility rather than acknowledging a data-query result.

The same background administration snapshots the node before taking a provider attempt. A snapshot/copy failure leaves its retryable entry uncompleted and publishes no durable failure marker; this void attempt helper is not a successful public read terminal.
Claim release treats unknown read outcome as not-gone and requeues invalidated work. It does not claim the unread body was absent or successfully processed.
Recent-processed validation marks a failed fresh read as not-same and removes the skip cache, forcing later work rather than falsely accepting a processed source revision.

A notification only prompts revision comparison. Unknown body reads retain the retry entry and active claim; only confirmed absence drops/invalidates them. Later claim/save source checks remain authoritative, so draining the notification cannot acknowledge stale work.

The existing DLQ retry owner retains the ID and deadline when a revision read is unknown, even if its duplicate MAIN marker is consumed. Independent retry wakeup and claim/save revision validation preserve the work; the fallback fresh scan does not publish a data result.
Graph rerank body refresh is optional: a failed refresh falls back to already materialized relationship/node candidate text. It does not create missing result entities or claim the refresh succeeded.

The queue originates from indexRelationship's owned edge copy. If an optional current read fails, that reported image can still be embedded; publication compares its source to the current entry and rejects superseded images. Provider failure requeues while the entry exists; no required public Search hydration is skipped.

MMR embedding refresh has an explicit original-score fallback with nil diversity vectors; canonical result hydration remains a separate required error-returning owner. Missing entities alone use the orphan policy.
Required stage-2 rerank content uses readSearchNode and returns rerankOutcome.failure, consumed by the existing Search coordinator and diagnostics. Qualified public Search green is retained.

All consumers request optional chunk placement/text annotations for an already required hydrated hit. Carried EmbedMeta is usable recovery; missing metadata yields documented null chunk locations or bounded carried property text. This helper never supplies node existence or the required matching properties.

Admin statistics returns an HTTP boundary error immediately when the issued per-database EdgeCount fails. Aggregate counters are updated only after both count reads succeed, so failed edge counts cannot appear as valid zero totals.

Admin statistics rejects a failed NodeCount with an HTTP error before reading or adding that database's totals. It preserves the manager's issued view and does not recover a native counter to evade admission.

Composite status is an explicit partial-diagnostic protocol: NodeCount failure sets partial=true and reachable=false with an error on the row. handleDatabaseInfo publishes the constituent error/partial status and does not claim aggregate search readiness; the count is not presented as a complete authoritative query result.

The composite diagnostic EdgeCount error follows the same explicit partial row protocol, retaining the edge cause unless the earlier node read also failed. The aggregate caller consumes partial; this differs from silently accepting a successful empty count result.
Ordinary database information returns a boundary HTTP error on the issued storage NodeCount failure before assembling its response. It cannot publish zero as a valid node count.

Ordinary database information independently checks EdgeCount and returns the boundary error before constructing a success response. Native/forwarded counter representation remains the maintainer's owner; this member only preserves its outcome.

The similarity endpoint maps a target point-read failure to an explicit HTTP not-found error under its existing target/visibility response policy. It emits no successful search result or empty hit list after the failed lookup; this code is not the Search hydration retry owner.

Native incoming-degree facade retains zero on failed countByPrefix and names GetIncomingEdges in its Deprecated doc. Internal uses are forbidden by the whole legacy class compiler population; TJ owns native count implementation.

Native outgoing-degree facade retains zero on failed countByPrefix and names GetOutgoingEdges in its Deprecated doc. This is an external compatibility provider, not an internal consumer; TJ owns native count implementation.

The pre-write DeleteEdge point read is a speculative publication image. The authoritative publishing transaction reloads edgeForAdjacency with errors, replaces edge with that image and requires deleteEdgeInTxn to succeed before publication. A failed speculative read is either recovered by the real write capture or the deletion fails; it cannot alone acknowledge a successful mutation.

Native GetAllNodes keeps its slice-only signature and existing omission behavior, with Deprecated documentation naming AllNodes; production internal consumer migration is checked by the whole-class gate.

Every compiled production reference identified so far is inside BadgerEngine.GetEdgeBetween, the explicitly retained errorless legacy facade. Its head/set/legacy retry helper implements that compatibility API, not an internal query consumer; whole-class compiler proof still required.

BadgerTransaction.GetAllNodes is the public compatibility facade over AllNodes and retains nil on error; its signature and body stay compatible and are documented Deprecated.
BadgerTransaction.GetEdgeBetween keeps nil-on-failure and type filtering as a legacy facade; error-aware internal readers must use GetEdgesBetween.

Change retention’s periodic job logs a prune failure with its database and retries on later ticks; RunOnce is a background maintenance callback, not a successful public read result. No error is converted into user query data.

ConstituentDatabaseForEdge is a public errorless point-backed metadata facade; its existing empty-on-failure behavior is Deprecated with GetEdge/Database as the error-aware route. Internal transport callers still need migration.
ConstituentDatabaseForNode is the corresponding public node-source facade; keep empty-on-failure compatibility, document GetNode/Database, and migrate internal transport consumers.

Write-owner hint refusal, required source admission and hard start/end lookup errors now return before trying another physical writer; only genuine not-found permits the existing later-source search. The public probe is being corrected to avoid assuming writable map iteration order.

Composite GetAllNodes keeps its slice-only facade and omission behavior over AllNodes; Deprecated documentation names the error-returning API.

Global label count is only a cost/admission hint for the direct label scan. A count failure makes labelCoversScope false, leaving the ordinary scope scan authoritative; it never publishes the failed count or an empty data collection.

The namespace total-count read is also an optional scan admission hint. If NodeCountByPrefix fails, labelCoversScope refuses that optimization and the normal read/error path remains responsible; no native count forwarding or representation is changed here.

The namespace label count contributes only to the same optimization boolean after a successful prefix count. Its error forces false, so it cannot convert a failed required data read into a handled empty result.

The verifier preserves the pending marker after unknown read failure and returns no claim, allowing the existing polling owner to retry. Only ErrNotFound retires the stale marker; public pending-retry controls passed on9120.
Remote GetAllNodes preserves the release empty slice on failure and is Deprecated in favor of AllNodes; the remote error-returning read owner remains unchanged.
Remote GetEdgeBetween retains nil on failed remote lookup and is Deprecated in favor of GetEdgesBetween plus type selection; no public signature change is introduced.

Remote GetInDegree is an exported legacy no-error API in the explicitly approved compatibility class. It retains release zero-on-failure behavior, is Deprecated with GetIncomingEdges as the error-carrying peer, and production callers must fail the whole-class reference/unavailability gate.

Remote GetOutDegree retains its patch-compatible scalar signature and zero-on-failure semantics, with a Deprecated comment naming GetOutgoingEdges. It is an external compatibility facade; the internal read population must consume the error-carrying adjacency owner.

copyEdgeWithContext allocates/copies existing body fields and maps, with copyContextError as its sole error source. A nil context disables those checks, so copyEdge cannot suppress a read/validation failure.
copyNodeWithContext composes existing field/map/vector copy owners; every returned error comes from copyContextError. Nil context cannot fail, and no second recursive property copier is introduced.
copyNodeWithoutEmbeddingsWithContext copies supplied fields/maps and returns only copyContextError. The nil-context facade cannot discard a storage read failure because it never reads storage.
perf_direct measures durations only for successful update samples and skips failed reads/updates. It is an operator benchmark sampling helper returning timings, not a database read-result API.
The cancellation test’s background read sends its error on done, the enclosing test receives it and requires success under a deadline. No test or public terminal silently loses that read error.
